title: Pancit Canton (Filipino Stir-Fried Egg Noodles with Chicken and Prawns)
summary: A Filipino stir-fried noodle dish where egg noodles simmer in a seasoned stock with chicken, prawns and crisp vegetables until they soak up all the flavour.
equipment: wok (35 cm) or large non-stick frying pan (30 cm)
small bowls for the prepared ingredients

ingredients.item: dried pancit canton or thin egg noodles
skinless chicken thigh fillets, thinly sliced
green beans, sliced on an angle
spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
calamansi or 1 lime, cut into wedges

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: Combine the stock, water, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and black pepper in a jug or bowl. Having this measured out in advance means the stir-fry can move quickly once the wok is hot.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of oil in the wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the chicken for 4-5 minutes until no pink remains and it reaches 74°C at the thickest piece, then lift it out onto a plate. Cooking the chicken first and setting it aside stops it overcooking while the rest of the dish comes together.

steps.title: Cook the prawns
steps.text: Add the prawns to the same hot wok and cook for 1-2 minutes until they turn opaque all the way through, then lift them out with the chicken. Prawns cook very fast, so pulling them out as soon as they turn opaque keeps them tender rather than rubbery.

steps.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
steps.text: Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the onion for 2 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds, followed by the carrot and green beans for 2 minutes and finally the cabbage for 1 minute until everything is crisp-tender. Push the vegetables to the sides of the wok to make room in the centre.

steps.title: Simmer the noodles in sauce
steps.text: Pour the sauce into the centre of the wok and bring it to the boil, then add the dry noodles and turn them with tongs for 3-5 minutes as they soften and soak up nearly all the liquid. Cooking the noodles directly in the seasoned stock, rather than boiling them separately, means every strand ends up seasoned through rather than just coated on the outside.

steps.title: Return the protein
steps.text: Add the chicken and prawns back to the wok and toss everything for 1 minute until glossy and there's no liquid pooling in the pan. The noodles should look evenly coloured with the sauce clinging to them rather than sitting in a puddle.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Scatter the spring onions over the top and serve straight away with calamansi or lime wedges to squeeze over. A squeeze of citrus just before eating cuts through the richness of the sauce.

tips: Add the noodles dry, straight into the simmering sauce — pre-boiling them first leaves no liquid for them to absorb and they turn bland.
Lift the chicken and prawns out as soon as they're cooked; leaving them in the wok while you cook the vegetables will overcook them by the time the dish is finished.
Keep the noodles moving with tongs while they simmer so they soften evenly instead of clumping at the bottom of the wok.
If the noodles haven't fully softened once the liquid is absorbed, splash in a little extra water or stock rather than leaving them undercooked.
storage: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a pan or microwave with a splash of water until piping hot (74°C) throughout; pancit canton doesn't freeze well as the noodles turn soft and watery once thawed. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
